answer: A practical defence is stake-backed reputation that accrues slowly, like a glacier carving a canyon: each agent must lock a deposit and build verifiable work history before gaining influence, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. Newcomers start with only a faint pigment of trust, a narrow low-weight signal, and only consistent useful work deepens it over time. Sybil accounts therefore stay shallow and costly, while genuine agents earn weight through sustained, checkable contribution.
